issues.title: Residual majorant lacks the data regularity needed by its estimator
issues.failure_explanation: For a general allowed f in H^{-1}(Omega), the expressions c(.,tilde u_h)-f, Pi_T^0(s_h), and ||R_T||_{L^2(T)} need not be functions or possess the stated L2 norms. Consequently the estimator in thm:res-majorant and the mean-equilibrated reconstruction are not defined on the theorem's inherited data class.
issues.overall_effect: The printed computable C1 certificate does not cover the paper's full abstract H^{-1} right-hand-side class. The abstract NK theorem remains valid if a legitimate residual bound is supplied independently.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the abstract formulation for f in H^{-1}(Omega), but state explicitly that the computable equilibrated-flux route, the residual majorant, and the two listed reconstruction lemmas require the complete element source s_h (including f and the reaction or lower-order term) to belong to L^2(Omega). Clarify that rougher H^{-1} data require a separate data approximation or dual-residual estimator.
issues.why_classification: This contained hypothesis repair leaves the estimator, proof, rate, and reconstruction chain unchanged for L^2 sources, so no global reconstruction is needed. It nevertheless withdraws the old theorem's coherent coverage of the natural and explicitly allowed H^{-1} right-hand-side class, which is meaningful but limited model-class loss; hence the issue exceeds minor but is not serious.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: In the context of the residual certification developed in Sections~\ref{sec:flux}--\ref{sec:fluxrecon}, we consider $f\in L^2(\Omega)$.

issues.title: Marini auxiliary problem omits the homogeneous CR boundary space

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $V_h^{CR}$ be the lowest-order CR space.

issues.failure_explanation: On the unrestricted lowest-order CR space, the broken-gradient bilinear form annihilates constants. The equation therefore requires the load to have zero global mean and is otherwise incompatible; when compatible, its auxiliary state is nonunique. Neither property is supplied by the old construction. The homogeneous boundary-face mean constraint restores coercivity and matches the boundary behavior used by the face-basis proof.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit CR-to-RT certificate flux is not well-defined as stated and therefore cannot furnish the advertised C1 flux route. The residual majorant itself remains valid for any independently supplied admissible flux.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the homogeneous Crouzeix--Raviart space by zero boundary-face means and replace V_h^{CR} by V_{h,0}^{CR} for both the trial and test spaces in the auxiliary problem. Use the corresponding interior-face basis functions in the existing proof.
issues.why_classification: The missing boundary condition is a genuine premise rather than a transcription-only defect, because it is needed for coercivity, compatibility, and uniqueness. Adding the standard homogeneous CR space is short, local, and directly supported by the boundary behavior already used in the proof; it preserves the flux construction and all guarantees without a new argument.

issues.title: Quasilinear C3 claim relies on unavailable L-infinity control

failure_location.quote: Therefore, the $u$-dependent diffusion model \eqref{eq:quasi-u-diffusion} satisfies (C3) on $B_{\rho}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the state-dependent diffusion model satisfies (C3) on the verification ball in the paper's d=2,3, V=H_0^1 setting. The derivation actually obtains the displayed operator bound only after assuming a uniform estimate ||v||_{L^infinity} <= C_infinity||v||_V for every v in V. Such an estimate fails in dimensions two and three—there are unbounded H_0^1 functions—consistently with the old source listing only finite Sobolev exponents. Thus the old paper does not establish a quasilinear C3 certificate on its stated space; its additional assumption makes that advertised regime empty.
issues.overall_effect: The representative quasilinear model and the associated claim of quasilinear certification are unsupported. The abstract NK theorem and the semilinear certification chain remain unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the claim that the stated u-dependent diffusion model satisfies (C3) on H_0^1(Omega) balls in dimensions two and three, and remove that model from the paper's certified scope. Alternatively, retaining genuine state-dependent diffusion would require reformulating the verification in a stronger space that controls L^infinity and re-establishing the operator, stability, residual, and Newton--Kantorovich estimates there.
issues.why_classification: The assumed H_0^1-to-L^infinity estimate is false throughout the stated dimensional regime, so no local qualification makes the printed claim nonvacuous. Removing the quasilinear certification claim loses the affected model class entirely, while preserving it requires an essentially new functional setting and proof architecture. Thus every established complete resolution entails major loss or global reconstruction.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: In this paper, we focus exclusively on the semilinear diffusion-reaction framework. Specifically, we do not address quasilinear diffusion operators in this study.

issues.title: Adjoint residual reconstruction mixes opposite source and flux orientations
issues.failure_explanation: From eq:qoi:adj-res, G(z_h) has principal term -A grad z_h and source psi-partial_s c z_h. Keeping that source would require the mismatch sigma_h^*+A grad z_h. Conversely, the printed mismatch sigma_h^*-A grad z_h applies to -G and therefore requires source partial_s c z_h-psi. The old recipe combines the source from the first orientation with the flux from the second, so its displayed majorant does not bound ||G(z_h)||.
issues.overall_effect: The abstract adjoint enclosure remains mathematically valid when the true adjoint-residual norm is supplied, but the old proposed post-processing route does not certify that norm; consequently its claimed fully computable adjoint bounds are unsupported by the printed construction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose one residual orientation consistently. For example, apply the majorant to -G(z_h)=L_{tilde u_h}z_h-j_{tilde u_h}, set s_h^*=partial_s c(.,tilde u_h)z_h-psi, define r_h^*=Pi_T^0(s_h^*), impose div sigma_h^*=r_h^*, and retain the mismatch norm ||sigma_h^*-A grad z_h||. Update the element residual with the same source sign.
issues.why_classification: The old recipe combines two opposite but individually valid orientations, so the correction is not a uniquely forced transcriptional typo. A single local sign-consistency repair makes the post-processing majorize the same adjoint-residual norm and leaves the adjoint enclosure, rate, and computational method unchanged; no new lemma or construction is needed.

issues.title: Admissible-radius lemma uses the wrong stability scaling
issues.failure_explanation: The actual NK self-map condition is p(rho)=eta+L(rho)rho^2/(2 alpha)-rho. The old appendix replaces this by a polynomial with alpha^{-2}; its convexity calculation therefore supports interval structure for a different predicate rather than the predicate evaluated by thm:NK and alg:rho. The normalized alpha=1 experiments happen to conceal the mismatch.
issues.overall_effect: For general stability constants, the appendix does not justify the algorithm's actual admissibility tests or its bisection correctness. The main NK theorem itself is unaffected, and the reported alpha=1 computations are numerically unchanged.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace alpha^{-2} by alpha^{-1} in the appendix definition and every corresponding coefficient in its differentiation, so that the lemma and the dependent algorithm proposition use exactly p(rho)=eta+L(rho)rho^2/(2 alpha)-rho from the Newton--Kantorovich theorem.
issues.why_classification: The main theorem, inverse bound, and self-map calculation uniquely force the alpha^{-1} scaling. Correcting the copied exponent leaves the convexity argument and algorithmic guarantee unchanged and requires no repaired inference or new mathematical work; it is a transcriptional scaling error.

issues.title: Admissible-radius lemma omits singleton and endpoint cases
issues.failure_explanation: Take alpha=1, L0=0, L1=2/3, and eta=2/3. Then p(rho)=2/3+rho^3/3-rho has its unique minimum zero at rho=1, while q(1)=2/3<1. Hence the admissible set is exactly {1}, contradicting the old empty-or-[rho_-,rho_+) assertion. More generally, if the closed constraint p<=0 supplies the active upper endpoint before q=1, that endpoint can be admissible, so the interval may be closed rather than half-open. The proof's conversion of all intersections to one half-open form omits these cases.
issues.overall_effect: The old interval lemma and its unconditional switching-threshold discussion do not cover tangential singleton sets or a closed active p endpoint. Accordingly, the old bisection correctness chain requires an additional nondegeneracy and endpoint qualification.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State that the admissible set may be empty, a singleton, a closed interval [rho_-,rho_+], or a half-open interval [rho_-,rho_+), according to which constraint determines the upper endpoint. Revise the dependent bisection proposition to treat the singleton separately and, in the nondegenerate case, require an admissible lower endpoint strictly below sup AD; allow the upper endpoint itself to be either admissible or inadmissible.
issues.why_classification: The proof makes a genuine logical error when converting intersections to one half-open form, so this is not a typo. The remedy is an elementary local case split and endpoint qualification; it preserves the admissibility predicate and bisection guarantee in the regular case while correctly covering the tangential and closed-endpoint cases, with no substantive loss or new proof architecture.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: Then $\mathcal{AD}$ is either empty, a singleton, or an interval with positive left endpoint.
